conclusion.summary: No single model wins every task. codellama:7b and phi3:mini both produced correct, grounded answers across all 12 questions with different strengths per category; starcoder2:3b (as pulled from Ollama's default tag) failed to genuinely answer any of the 12 questions in any category -- it repeatedly generated new fake questions instead of responding, indicating it is a base/completion-style model rather than instruction-tuned like the other two. Raw speed is therefore not a valid quality signal on its own: starcoder2:3b was the fastest model (18.7s avg) but delivered zero usable answers.

category_winners.reason: More consistent answer length/detail across both explanation questions; phi3:mini was excellent on the short question but became very verbose on the longer one without adding proportional value.
Gave a direct, minimal, fully correct answer ('File: auth.py'); codellama:7b was technically correct but phrased it confusingly.
Stayed on-topic throughout; phi3:mini's answer drifted into unrelated generated text at the end (mild hallucination/prompt-leakage).
codellama:7b gave an internally contradictory answer on one question; phi3:mini's reasoning was clearer and consistent on both.
codellama:7b's generated unit test contained a subtle bug (comparing a real hash to a literal placeholder string, which would fail if run); phi3:mini's generated test looked structurally correct.
Both suggested valid, comparable improvements (stronger hashing algorithms, salting) with no meaningful quality difference.
More concise and precise, e.g. explicitly naming both required conditions for a successful payment.

limitations: Dataset size: 12 questions (covering all 7 required categories plus repository understanding) instead of the suggested 20-30. On this CPU-only VM each answer took roughly 15-120 seconds, so 20-30 questions x 3 models would have meant 60-90 model calls and several hours of runtime; 12 questions (36 calls) kept the run feasible while still giving every category at least one question. Categories with a single question (Code Retrieval, Dependency Understanding, Code Generation, Refactoring) should therefore be read as indicative rather than statistically conclusive.
CPU/memory consumption was observed at the VM level (all models are served by one shared Ollama process) rather than measured separately per model and per question.
Code test-pass rate was judged by inspecting the generated tests against the real functions, not by executing them.
Correctness and hallucination verdicts are manual judgments by the group, made by comparing each answer to the actual source files.
conclusion.overall_recommendation: For this application, phi3:mini offers the best practical trade-off: essentially the same real-world answer quality as codellama:7b, at meaningfully lower average latency (40.5s vs 50.1s) on this CPU-only VM. codellama:7b remains a strong alternative where slightly higher precision matters (Explanation, Dependency Understanding, RAG-based questions). starcoder2:3b, in its default Ollama configuration, is not usable for this application at all -- it would need a different (instruction-tuned) tag or model to be considered.

metric_definitions.correctness: Manually judged by comparing the model's answer against the actual sample_codebase source files. Scored as: correct (fully matches the real code/logic), partial (mostly right but has an imprecision, hedge, or a subtly wrong detail), or incorrect/no_answer (wrong, contradictory, or did not actually respond to the question).
metric_definitions.hallucination: Flagged true if the answer states something not present in / contradicted by the actual codebase (e.g. inventing a file, function, or fact that doesn't exist), or if the model ignored the question and generated unrelated text instead.
metric_definitions.relevance: Whether the answer actually addresses the specific question asked, using the retrieved context, rather than giving a generic or off-topic response.
metric_definitions.retrieval_quality: Whether the top-2 chunks returned by the Retrieval Service (cosine similarity over embeddings) actually contained the information needed to answer the question correctly.
metric_definitions.test_pass_rate: For code_generation questions only: whether the generated test/code would actually run correctly against the real functions (checked by manual inspection, not execution, given time constraints).
metric_definitions.response_latency: Wall-clock time in seconds from sending the prompt to Ollama's /api/generate endpoint to receiving the full (non-streamed) response, measured in the evaluation script.
metric_definitions.token_usage: The eval_count field returned by Ollama's API for each response -- the number of tokens the model generated for that answer.
metric_definitions.resource_consumption: All three models run via the same Ollama process on the same CPU-only VM (8GB RAM, 2 vCPU) -- resource use was observed via `docker stats` / `ollama ps` during the largest model (codellama:7b) generation (peaked near 100% of one CPU core, ~4-5GB RAM while the model was loaded), rather than isolated per-model, since Ollama serves one model at a time from a shared process on this hardware.
